seo.ogTitle: House Cleanouts in Mobile, AL — Zoiris Junk Removal
seo.ogDescription: Room-by-room or whole-home clearing in Mobile, Alabama: attics, closets, spare rooms, furniture, and appliances.

purpose: Serve Mobile homeowners who need several rooms or a whole house cleared at once, such as before listing a home, after years of accumulation, ahead of a remodel, or when the home is cluttered past the point of a single pickup. Unlike estate cleanouts, the person booking usually lives in the home or owns it outright.

content.lead: A house cleanout is for when the problem is bigger than one couch or one closet. Zoiris Junk Removal clears multiple rooms, or an entire house, in Mobile, Alabama. That can mean attic boxes, spare-room furniture, old appliances, and years of accumulated clutter. You choose the rooms and the items, and we plan the job so it moves through the house in a sensible order.

quickAnswer.question: Can you clear out a whole house in one visit?
quickAnswer.answer: Often, yes, but it depends on how much is in the house. Send photos of each room, the attic, and the garage, and we will tell you up front whether the job fits in one visit or needs more than one. Nothing goes on the calendar until you have agreed to the estimate and the pickup window.

includes.heading: What a house cleanout includes
includes.intro: A house cleanout is planned around the whole home, not a single item. That typically means:
points: Clearing rooms in an order that keeps hallways open, usually starting with upper floors and the rooms farthest from the door.
Bringing down attic contents that you can reach from a pull-down ladder or stairs, such as boxes, old luggage, and stored furniture.
Emptying closets, spare bedrooms, sunrooms, and porches of unwanted items.
Removing large household appliances that are already disconnected.
Taking out rolled carpet and rugs if you have pulled them up, so floors are ready for the next step.

items.heading: What a typical house cleanout removes
items.intro: Most household contents qualify. Items marked "call to confirm" need a quick check before scheduling.
list: Living room and bedroom furniture: sofas, recliners, dressers, and nightstands
Mattresses and box springs from every bedroom
Boxes, bags, and bins of stored household goods
Toys, décor, holiday decorations, and housewares
Rolled carpet, padding, and area rugs
Kitchen and garage refrigerators or freezers — call to confirm

audience.heading: When people book a house cleanout
body: The most common reasons are getting a house ready to sell or rent, clearing space before a renovation, and tackling a home that has filled up over decades. Some people are downsizing and need to empty the bigger house before they move into the smaller one.

If you are clearing a loved one's home after a death or a move into care, our [estate cleanouts](/services/estate-cleanouts/) page covers how we work with families. Landlords and realtors handling a vacant rental should see [property cleanouts](/services/property-cleanouts/).

process.heading: How we plan a house cleanout

steps.title: Room-by-room photos
steps.body: Send a [pickup request](/request-pickup/) with photos of each room you want cleared, plus the attic and garage if they are included. Note any rooms that should be left untouched.

steps.title: Scope and schedule
steps.body: We size the job, tell you whether it is one visit or several, and confirm an estimate and a pickup window. For big homes, we may suggest starting with the fullest rooms.

steps.title: Top to bottom
steps.body: The crew works from the top floor and back rooms toward the front door, so the carry path stays clear and finished rooms stay finished.

steps.title: Walk the house
steps.body: When the truck is loaded, walk through with us. Anything we missed, or anything you decided to add at the last minute, gets sorted out then.

pricingFactors.heading: What affects the cost of a house cleanout
pricingFactors.intro: There is no flat rate for a whole house, so we quote each one based on what is actually there:
factors: Total volume across all rooms, attic, and garage
Number of floors and how many items must come down stairs
Attic access — a walk-up attic is simpler than a narrow pull-down hatch
Heavy appliances and furniture compared with light boxed items
Whether the job is done in one visit or split into phases

prepare.heading: Getting the house ready
tips: Pick a tape color for things that stay, and mark them before we arrive. One color for the whole house keeps it simple.
Close the doors to rooms we should skip, and tell us which ones they are.
Pull anything you want from the attic first, or tell us which boxes to bring down for you to check.
Unplug appliances and empty the refrigerator. Gas stoves and dryers must be disconnected by a qualified person before pickup.
Check closets, under beds, and the backs of cabinets for keepsakes, cash, and paperwork.
If you have pets, plan to keep them in a closed room or out of the house during the cleanout.

restrictions.heading: Before you book
restrictions.body: A few situations need to be discussed before we schedule a house cleanout:
list: Homes with heavy accumulation are fine to call about. Telling us honestly how full the house is helps us plan the right size of job.
Pest problems, mold, or water damage should be mentioned up front so we can plan handling.
Built-in cabinets, fixtures, or flooring that still has to be torn out falls under [construction debris removal](/services/construction-debris-removal/), and we do not do demolition.
Chemicals, paint, propane, and fuel are not accepted. Neither are medications or sharps.

faqs.q: Do I need to be home during the cleanout?
faqs.a: It helps to be there at the start to walk the crew through what stays and what goes. After that, many homeowners leave us to work and come back for the final walk-through.

faqs.q: Can you leave some rooms completely alone?
faqs.a: Yes. Tell us which rooms are off-limits when you book, and keep those doors closed on the day. We will only work in the rooms you have included.

faqs.q: The house is very cluttered. Is that a problem?
faqs.a: No. Heavily filled homes are exactly what house cleanouts are for. Photos and an honest description help us decide whether to plan a single visit or a series of visits, and we will never judge the state of a home.

faqs.q: We are listing the house soon. Can you clear it before photos?
faqs.a: Tell us your listing or photo date when you call, and we will confirm a pickup window that fits around it if one is available. Booking early gives you the most options.

faqs.q: Should I rent a dumpster instead?
faqs.a: A dumpster means you do the lifting and it sits in your driveway. A cleanout means our crew carries everything out. Our [junk removal vs. dumpster rental](/guides/junk-removal-vs-dumpster-rental/) guide compares the two.
